symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of vertices in the fixed experimental network.

symbols.name: \mathbb A
symbols.def: The two exposure labels \(\mathbb A=\{1,0\}\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic label, with \(a=1\) denoting the focal exposure and \(a=0\) denoting the comparison exposure.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The fixed adjacency matrix on the \(n\) experimental units.

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: The randomization distribution chosen before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: The treatment vector drawn from \(\nu\).

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: The exposure mapping induced by \(G\) for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y_i(w)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(w\).

symbols.name: D_{i,a}
symbols.def: The indicator \(D_{i,a}=\mathbf 1\{f_i(W)=a\}\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The vector \(D=(D_{1,1},\ldots,D_{n,1},D_{1,0},\ldots,D_{n,0})^{\top}\).

symbols.name: \pi_{i,a}
symbols.def: The known probability \(\pi_{i,a}=\mathbb E_{\nu}[D_{i,a}]\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: The diagonal matrix whose diagonal is \((\pi_{1,1},\ldots,\pi_{n,1},\pi_{1,0},\ldots,\pi_{n,0})\).

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: The known matrix \(\Omega=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(D)\).

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The superpopulation law of the pair \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) used only for ex ante basis choice.

symbols.name: F_a
symbols.def: The marginal law of \(Y_i(a)\) under \(H\).

symbols.name: F_1
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=1\).

symbols.name: F_0
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=0\).

symbols.name: \Gamma(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The class \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)=\{H\in\mathcal P([0,1]^2):\operatorname{marg}(H)=(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: F_a^{-1}
symbols.def: The generalized inverse of the marginal distribution function.

symbols.name: \mu_a
symbols.def: The mean \(\mu_a=\int y\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \sigma_a^2
symbols.def: The variance \(\sigma_a^2=\int(y-\mu_a)^2\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The covariance image \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=\{\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: The scalar \(c=\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) for \(H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).

symbols.name: Q(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the matrix \(Q(c)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_1^2I_n&-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n\\-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n&\mu_0^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_0^2I_n\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: b_1
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the focal-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the comparison-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The matrix \(B(b_1,b_0)=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: S_B
symbols.def: The matrix \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the normalized smallest eigenvalue of \(S_B\).

symbols.name: \widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z
symbols.def: The block-separable matrices (B) satisfying (B^{\top}Omega Bsucc0); this is only the rank-two restriction of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain.

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z
symbols.def: The projective quotient of (\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
symbols.def: The compact normalized subclass with \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)\ge\kappa\).

symbols.name: g_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the Zhao gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]\).

symbols.name: \ell_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the residual \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\).

symbols.name: r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: w(B)
symbols.def: The primary loss \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: v^\star
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic correspondence \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\) on the fixed normalized regular projective class; it is not Zhao's optimizer correspondence on the published unquotiented domain.

symbols.name: m_a
symbols.def: The number of independent unpaired pilot outcomes observed under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: Y^{P}_{j,a}
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th independent pilot draw from \(F_a\), with no cross-arm pairing.

symbols.name: \widehat F_a
symbols.def: The empirical law \(\widehat F_a=m_a^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_a}\delta_{Y^P_{j,a}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic obtained by substituting empirical marginal moments and endpoints into \(r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The requested numerical optimality gap.

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: An exact rational or real-algebraic encoding, or certified inclusion-oracle encoding with effective refinement moduli and exact feasibility decisions, of the known design matrices, both endpoint moment matrices, endpoint covariances, regularity threshold, and tolerance.

symbols.name: h_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The maximum projective-chart diameter of a box retained at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: The instance \(\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) with \(G\) and the exposure maps held fixed.

symbols.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
symbols.def: The relatively topologized class of instances satisfying the named predicates ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: The causal contrast \(\tau=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}\).

symbols.name: h(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: B_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: An exactly feasible basis used to certify an upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: L_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational lower bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obtained from outward-rounded lower bounds over all retained feasible boxes.

symbols.name: U_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) certified by an exactly feasible incumbent and outward rounding.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\varepsilon
symbols.def: The union of unpruned quotient-chart boxes, required to contain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A checkable record of the chart cover, feasible incumbent, minimization bounds, retained outer boxes, exact infeasibility or lower-bound pruning records, and mesh.

symbols.name: \Delta(\xi)
symbols.def: The gap \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive certified lower bound on \(\Delta(\xi)\).

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: A uniform positive lower bound on normalized nondegeneracy above \(\kappa\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).

symbols.name: \widehat w(B)
symbols.def: The endpoint residual criterion obtained by substituting the empirical marginal moments and Frechet covariance endpoints into \(w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z^+
symbols.type: projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain
symbols.def: The note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable positive-semidefinite pseudoinverse carrier, including ranks zero, one, and two.

symbols.name: S_B^+
symbols.def: Zhao's positive-semidefinite spectral inverse of (S_B=B^{\top}Omega B), taking reciprocal positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues.

symbols.name: g_B^+(c)
symbols.def: The Zhao-form pseudoinverse gain evaluated on the note's quotient (\mathcal B_Z^+).

symbols.name: \ell_B^+(c)
symbols.def: The residual (h(c)-g_B^+(c)) on the note's quotient of Zhao's published carrier.

symbols.name: w^+(B)
symbols.def: The maximum of (\ell_B^+(c_L)) and (\ell_B^+(c_U)) on (\mathcal B_Z^+).

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
symbols.def: The infimum of (w^+(B)) over the note's projective quotient (\mathcal B_Z^+); it need not be attained.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
symbols.def: The possibly empty set of classes in (\mathcal B_Z^+) satisfying (w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0^+
symbols.def: The possibly empty argmax of (g_B^+(0)) over the note's quotient (\mathcal B_Z^+).

symbols.name: \iota
symbols.type: rank-two inclusion into the full quotient
symbols.def: The bijection from the ordinary rank-two projective class (\mathcal B_Z) onto the rank-two stratum of the note's quotient (\mathcal B_Z^+).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)
symbols.def: The set \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\) with the threshold shown explicitly.

symbols.name: Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: The realized outcome \(Y_i(W)\) in the main experiment.

symbols.name: \widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: The vector with entries \(D_{i,1}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,1}\) in the first block and \(-D_{i,0}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,0}\) in the second block.

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
symbols.def: The coefficient (S_B^+B^{\top}OmegaPi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}), equal to the ordinary-inverse formula on the regular rank-two class.

symbols.name: \widehat 1_a
symbols.def: The average \(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), when its denominator is positive.

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)
symbols.def: The armwise self-normalized version of Zhao's pseudoinverse Horvitz--Thompson coefficient.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
symbols.def: The Horvitz--Thompson exposure-effect estimator minus the chosen coefficient times the centered basis exposure statistic.

symbols.name: \mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}
symbols.type: reproducible unexecuted heuristic Jiangxi PICC reanalysis protocol
symbols.def: The checked local-Adam, positive-definite rank-two, ordinary-solve and self-normalized protocol; no numerical table or global certificate is asserted.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The vector \(Y=(Y_1(1),\ldots,Y_n(1),-Y_1(0),\ldots,-Y_n(0))^{\top}\).

symbols.name: q_Z
symbols.def: The map \(q_Z(B)=[B]\) that quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two arm columns.

symbols.name: \overline a
symbols.def: A fixed uniform bound on every coordinate of a normalized supplied basis.

symbols.name: \mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
symbols.def: The intersection of \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) with the coordinate envelope indexed by \(\overline a\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The exponent governing the maximum dependency-neighborhood size.

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: The exponent governing decay of the minimum exposure probability.

symbols.name: \underline\pi
symbols.def: The constant in the lower bound \(\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).

symbols.name: \overline d
symbols.def: The constant in the maximum closed-neighborhood bound \(\overline d n^{\alpha}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal G_n
symbols.def: A graph whose separated coordinate sets index independent subvectors of \(D\).

symbols.name: \widehat Q_e
symbols.def: The plug-in endpoint matrix obtained from the two empirical pilot marginals.

symbols.name: C_n
symbols.def: The nuclear-norm sensitivity coefficient in lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate.

symbols.name: \widehat g_B(c)
symbols.def: The gain obtained by replacing the endpoint moment matrix by its pilot plug-in counterpart.

symbols.name: \widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: A measurable minimizer of the plug-in worst-endpoint loss.

symbols.name: \widehat B_0
symbols.def: A measurable maximizer of the plug-in zero-covariance gain.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}
symbols.def: The control-variate estimator formed with \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)\), kept separate from the primary Horvitz--Thompson-coefficient estimator.

symbols.name: \gamma_B^*(Y)
symbols.def: The coefficient \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}
symbols.def: The observable-map estimator with \(\gamma_B^*(Y)\) substituted for the estimated coefficient.

symbols.name: c_H
symbols.def: The covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The joint product law of the two independent arm-specific pilot samples.

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
symbols.def: The minimum of \(w(B)\) over \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{0,\overline a}
symbols.def: The argmax of \(g_B(0)\) over the rate-admissible class.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: The matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix}\) satisfying \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).

symbols.name: A_B
symbols.def: The matrix \(\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).

symbols.name: a_B
symbols.def: The zero-covariance gain \(g_B(0)\).

symbols.name: b_B
symbols.def: The coefficient of \(c\) in \(g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc\).

symbols.name: p_\xi(b)
symbols.def: The maximum of \((2/n-b)c_L\) and \((2/n-b)c_U\).

symbols.name: a^\star
symbols.def: The attained maximum of \(a_B\) over \(\mathcal B_Z\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{0,Z}
symbols.def: The argmax of \(a_B\) over \(\mathcal B_Z\), when attained.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}
symbols.def: The argmin of \(w(B)\) over \(\mathcal B_Z\), when attained.

symbols.name: \Delta_Z
symbols.def: The worst-loss difference between the best zero-covariance optimizer and the ordinary-domain minimax value, when the extrema are attained.

symbols.name: \varepsilon_m
symbols.def: A deterministic or pilot-measurable positive tolerance for full-carrier empirical minimization.

symbols.name: \widehat w_m^+(B)
symbols.def: The projector/pseudoinverse worst-endpoint loss obtained by substituting the two unpaired-pilot endpoint matrices, kept distinct from the regular rank-two objective (\widehat w(B)).

symbols.name: \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+
symbols.def: The fixed lexicographic selector satisfying (\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m).

assumptions.condition: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
For every unit \(i\), \(D_{i,1}D_{i,0}=0\) holds \(\nu\)-almost surely.
For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed potential-outcome pairs, Zhao Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22

assumptions.condition: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).
The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).

standard.name: Sharp Fréchet covariance range, Aronow--Green--Lee Lemma 1

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

standard.name: Independent product coupling with zero covariance

assumptions.condition: The basis satisfies \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).
The matrix \(S_B\) satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(S_B)>0\).

standard.name: Supplied-basis control-variate nondegeneracy, Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

novel.justification: Independent rescaling of either basis column leaves Zhao's control-variate span and gain unchanged, so this condition selects compact representatives without restricting implementable estimators.

assumptions.condition: The normalized covariance scale satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)\ge\kappa\).

standard.name: Supplied-basis nondegeneracy, fixed-threshold variant of Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

novel.justification: This is a verifiable design-side condition: for a fixed network, exposure maps, and known randomization, the matrix \(\Omega\) is known before outcomes are observed, so nonemptiness of the normalized \(\kappa\)-regular projective class can be certified as part of design preparation. Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) regulates a supplied basis and does not assert existence of such a normalized feasible basis.

assumptions.condition: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

novel.justification: Separate exposure-specific historical samples are available in insurance and public-health deployments even when privacy or record linkage prevents cross-arm pairing; independence from the later randomized assignment is ensured by collecting or freezing those archives before randomization. Mikhaeil and Green inform consistency of empirical marginal endpoints, not this product sampling law.

assumptions.condition: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.
There are constants \(\underline\pi>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that \(\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).

There is a dependency graph \(\mathcal G_n\) for the \(2n\) coordinates of \(D\): whenever two disjoint coordinate sets have no edge between them, their indicator subvectors are independent under \(\nu\); and there are constants \(\overline d<\infty\) and \(\alpha\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that every closed graph neighborhood has size at most \(\overline d n^{\alpha}\).
The nonnegative design-rate exponents satisfy \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\).
The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).

novel.justification: standard: independent external-pilot or sample-splitting condition

assumptions.condition: There exist \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that, for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\), \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\), \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), and \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\).

novel.justification: novel: a finite-dimensional design-side feasibility condition checkable before outcomes from the known \(\Omega\), \(\kappa\), and \(\overline a\); existence is not attributed to Zhao.

definitions.name: \Gamma(F_1,F_0)
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)=\{H\in\mathcal P([0,1]^2):\operatorname{marg}(H)=(F_1,F_0)\}\), the class carved by ass:fixed-marginals.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.

definitions.name: Q(c)
definitions.construction: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), \(Q(c)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_1^2I_n&-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n\\-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n&\mu_0^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_0^2I_n\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb S_+^{2n}\).

definitions.name: h(c),g_B(c),\ell_B(c)
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
definitions.construction:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z^+
definitions.construction:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).

definitions.name: \widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z,q_Z
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the unquotiented positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's published pseudoinverse basis domain, not the full published domain.  Define \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\), where \(\mathcal B_Z\) is its quotient by independent nonzero arm-column rescaling.

definitions.name: g_B^+(c),\ell_B^+(c),w^+(B),v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
definitions.construction:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.

definitions.name: w^+(B),v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+,w(B),v_{\mathrm{mm}},r(B),v^\star
definitions.construction: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.

definitions.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+,\mathcal A_0^+,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}},\mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_0
definitions.construction:
On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), define the primary full-quotient equality correspondences
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0),
\]
which may be empty.  On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction retain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\), and \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as regular deployable correspondences.

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
definitions.construction: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

definitions.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

definitions.name: projective interval branch-and-bound procedure
definitions.construction: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

definitions.name: \widehat w_m^+,\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+,\widehat w,\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}},\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) by a fixed rank-pattern and signed-chart lexicographic rule among bases satisfying
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le
\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]
Such a basis exists for every \(\varepsilon_m>0\) by the defining property of the infimum; no exact full-class argmin is assumed.  On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The full-class epsilon selector and the regular rank-two exact argmin are not conflated.

definitions.name: \Delta(\xi)
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).  Since every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), the second term equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\).

definitions.name: finite lawful minimax separation handle
definitions.construction: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and analyze simultaneously the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance-surrogate correspondences.  The instance-specific certificate consists of exact optimizer equality sets, a rational lower bound \(\delta>0\) on \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and a rational optimizer-wide regularity slack \(\eta>0\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).  This finite lawful separation handle is distinct from, and does not assert, generic finite-\(\varepsilon\) termination of the moment-complete projective interval branch-and-bound procedure.

definitions.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}},\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}},\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
definitions.construction:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^+=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\), so these maps reduce to the ordinary-inverse rank-two formulas used by the finite-rate results.  Separately define \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\) and zero otherwise, and obtain \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) by substitution.  No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.  The expectation identity needed for the oracle comparison is not built into this definition; it is derived from ass:known-exposure in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence.

definitions.name: \mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}
definitions.construction: The exploratory record \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}\) is the reproducible but unexecuted procedure implemented by \(\texttt{discovery/jiangxi\_robust\_reanalysis.py}\).  Its input directory must contain \(\texttt{survey.tab}\) and \(\texttt{network.tab}\).  The procedure cleans identifiers, sentinel \(99\), self-loops, and duplicate directed nominations while retaining cross-village nominations; constructs the three target populations for \(\tau_{10},\tau_{21},\tau_{32}\); and uses the disclosed independent Bernoulli \((1/2)\) reconstruction necessitated by the unreleased original strata.  It splits connected components of the exposure-overlap graph without cutting components and estimates the two marginal laws and Fr\'echet endpoints on each training fold.  The checked script is a heuristic positive-definite rank-two procedure: it normalizes two nonzero columns, evaluates ordinary inverses with \(\texttt{torch.linalg.solve}\) or \(\texttt{np.linalg.solve}\), penalizes small eigenvalues, and conducts local Adam searches under common initialization and iteration budgets.  It does not admit singular strata, use a Moore--Penrose or CAD solver, certify epsilon-global optimality, or check a declared coordinate envelope or \(\kappa\)-feasibility restriction.  Its held-out deployment uses the armwise self-normalized coefficient \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)\) and hence the implementation variant \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\).  Output fields report point estimates, both endpoint losses, worst loss, a minimum-eigenvalue diagnostic, and plug-in standard-error and objective diagnostics.  The standard-error field is not asserted to be an exact fixed-array design-randomization standard error, and the objective diagnostic is not a certified optimization gap.  Authenticated replication data were unavailable in the solve environment, so the protocol was not executed and no numerical table is asserted.  Its internal cross-fitting is distinct from the independent unpaired pilot of ass:unpaired-pilot, so neither the external-pilot first-order transfer theorem nor the full-class CAD guarantee is claimed for this application protocol.

definitions.name: \widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}},\widehat B_0
definitions.construction:
Under ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, and using only the independent unpaired pilot, define the regular rank-two selectors
\[
\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),
\qquad
\widehat B_0
\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0)
\]
by the fixed lexicographic quotient-chart tie-breaking rule.  In the independent main experiment deploy \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) through def:observable-coefficient-map.  On this class Zhao's published pseudoinverse equals the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.  The existence and measurability of these selectors are derived in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer; no out-of-class fallback is part of the construction.  This construction is the regular deployable restriction, not the primary full-class epsilon-minimizer rule.

definitions.name: a_B,b_B,p_\xi,\Delta_Z
definitions.construction:
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), define the ordinary-domain intercept and slope
\[
a_B=g_B(0),
\qquad
b_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\qquad g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc,
\]
and define the endpoint drift penalty
\[
p_\xi(b)=\max\{(2/n-b)c_L,(2/n-b)c_U\}.
\]
Whenever the relevant ordinary-domain extrema are attained, put
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\]
\[
\Delta_Z=
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B_0)
-\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
These objects use only the positive-definite ordinary-inverse domain; no singular or Moore--Penrose class is included.

statements.statement: Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures and ass:exposure-positivity, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.
statements.justification: The theorem imports the published Fréchet range and proves its exact affine reduction inside Zhao's basis objective.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1, already gives the sharp covariance range. Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23, gives the covariance-dependent basis objective, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 substitutes the feasible zero-covariance surrogate matrix; neither source derives the affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside this projective objective.
statements.consumer: An experimenter with only two pilot marginals can evaluate the exact worst-copula gain of any proposed network basis.

statements.statement:
For every \(\kappa>0\), the quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) has normalized representatives belonging to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\), so
\[
\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z,
\qquad
q_Z^{-1}\!\left(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa\right)=\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z.
\]
Thus the threshold classes exhaust the positive-definite rank-two projective restriction of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, modulo the exact independent nonzero column-rescaling fibers of \(q_Z\).  Each fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is threshold restricted, and ranks zero and one in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) are outside this proposition.
statements.justification: The proposition states exactly how compact threshold classes exhaust the maximal ordinary-inverse Zhao-type matrix domain modulo rescaling.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates regulates a supplied basis but does not construct the compact projective threshold exhaustion or prove its exact transfer back to all ordinary-invertible matrix representatives.
statements.consumer: A global solver can report its threshold while retaining a certified statement about the full ordinary-inverse matrix domain modulo rescaling.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(K_\kappa\) be the set of pairs \((b_1,b_0)\) satisfying the two sphere normalizations and \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^\top\Omega B)\ge\kappa\).  It is closed in a product of compact spheres.  Its quotient by the residual independent sign changes is therefore compact and equals \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Every member satisfies \(B^\top\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2\succ0\), hence lies in the positive-definite rank-two restriction \(\mathcal B_Z\) of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain.

Conversely, if \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), both arm columns are nonzero.  With
\[
T=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_1\rVert_2},
\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_0\rVert_2}\right),
\]
the representative \(BT\) is normalized and \(T^\top B^\top\Omega BT\succ0\).  Thus \(\rho_B=\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}(BT)^\top\Omega(BT)\}>0\), and \([B]\in\mathcal B_{\rho_B/2}\).  Hence \(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z\).  Surjectivity and the exact fibers of \(q_Z\), proved in thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer, give the inverse-image equality.  This exhausts only the positive-definite rank-two restriction; ranks zero and one remain in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\) and there is \(\eta>0\) such that \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), then there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
statements.justification: Persistence upgrades any exact finite witness from a curiosity to a nondegenerate region of lawful experiments.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals gives continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, while GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust gives a general dependence-robust decision template; neither proves strict robust-basis dominance for Zhao's optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: Any certified output of oeq:separated-lawful-witness with \(\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\) activates this theorem and yields a relative-open region on which every robust optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer.

statements.statement: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}\to v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely.  Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely in the projective quotient.
statements.justification: The set-valued conclusion is the strongest valid generic guarantee when projective symmetries or endpoint ties create multiple optimizers.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance and MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment prove scalar endpoint consistency; Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 3, concerns estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics but does not establish uniform global basis-objective or argmax-correspondence consistency.
statements.consumer: An independent historical or external pilot can select a robust network basis without pretending that its two marginal samples identify a cross-world copula.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:kappa-feasibility and prop:kappa-exhaustion, \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is a nonempty compact metrizable quotient.  Its representatives satisfy
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt n,
\qquad \lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
The armwise bounded strong law gives weak convergence of \(\widehat F_a\) to \(F_a\), convergence of the first two moments, and
\[
\int_0^1|\widehat F_a^{-1}(u)-F_a^{-1}(u)|\,du\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
The identity behind (2) is equality between the \(L^1\) distance of distribution functions and that of quantiles on the line.  Because all quantiles lie in \([0,1]\),
\[
|xy-x'y'|\le|x-x'|+|y-y'|
\]
shows that both empirical quantile-coupling cross moments converge.  Hence
\[
\widehat c_L\to c_L,\quad \widehat c_U\to c_U,\quad
\rho_m:=\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0
\tag{3}
\]
almost surely.

Exposure positivity fixes a finite \(\Pi^{-1}\).  Trace and operator-norm inequalities, together with (1), give a constant \(K<\infty\) depending only on the fixed design and \(\kappa\) such that
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\le K\rho_m\to0
\tag{4}
\]
almost surely.  Explicitly, the uncontrolled trace contributes at most \(2n^{-1}\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m\), and the two-dimensional gain trace contributes at most \(2\lVert\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2(n^2\kappa)^{-1}\rho_m\).

Both criteria are continuous on the compact quotient, so the population and empirical minima are attained.  The elementary inequality between two infima gives
\[
|\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}|
\le\sup_B|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and a subsequence converges to \(B_\infty\), then for any \(B^\star\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), empirical optimality and (4) give
\[
w(B_m)\le w(B^\star)+2\sup_B|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|.
\]
Passing to the limit proves \(w(B_\infty)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), hence \(B_\infty\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  This is the asserted outer limit on the fixed-\(\kappa\) rank-two restriction; no cross-rank conclusion is used. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.
statements.justification: This proposition draws the exact line between defensible set consistency and unjustified point consistency.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals implies upper hemicontinuity for optimizer sets but does not give this pilot-based quotient-space selection result or its tie counterexample.
statements.consumer: Applied reporting can retain all empirically indistinguishable robust bases unless an isolated unique saddle is actually verified.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Work on the probability-one event from thm:plugin-correspondence.  If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) and a measurable selection does not converge to \(B^\star\), a subsequence remains outside some neighborhood of \(B^\star\).  Compactness supplies a convergent further subsequence, and the outer-limit theorem forces its limit to equal \(B^\star\), a contradiction.

For the converse witness, take \(n=3\), \(f_i(w)=w_i\), independent Bernoulli \((1/2)\) assignment, \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\), and \(\kappa=1/8\).  Then
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12I_6,
\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad Q(0)=\widehat Q(0)=0.
\]
Thus \(w=\widehat w=0\) on all of \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The distinct projective bases
\[
B^{(2)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_2),
\qquad B^{(3)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_3)
\]
both have \(S_B=3I_2/4\) and are feasible.  Alternating between them according to the parity of the common pilot size is a measurable empirical minimizer selection with no point limit, while the outer-set conclusion holds exactly. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\{(b_1,b_0):\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ B^{\top}\Omega B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty.  It is closed in a product of two spheres and hence compact; prop:kappa-exhaustion identifies its finite sign quotient with \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  On (1),
\[
\lVert(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The trace formulas in def:gain-loss, the resolvent identity, and (2) make both endpoint losses, and hence their maximum \(w\), continuous on \(K_\kappa\).  The refinement moduli in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) turn this compactness argument into an effective uniform-continuity modulus: for every positive rational \(\rho\), the inclusion oracles terminate with a rational chart diameter \(d(\rho)>0\) such that two feasible representatives in the same box of diameter at most \(d(\rho)\) have losses differing by at most \(\rho\).

Cover each normalized projective factor by the finitely many signed pivot charts in def:branch-bound-handle.  Fix a rational \(\rho>0\) with \(4\rho<\varepsilon\), and bisect all retained boxes until their diameters are at most \(\min\{\varepsilon,d(\rho)\}\).  This is a finite depth and produces finitely many boxes.  The exact feasibility interface decides every box, including boxes whose feasible intersection lies entirely on
\(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  In each feasible box, exact feasible-child selection and repeated nested refinement give the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible point \(B_C\).  The endpoint inclusion oracles and their effective arithmetic moduli then terminate with outward rational bounds \(\underline q_C,\overline q_C\) satisfying
\[
w(B_C)-\rho\le\underline q_C\le w(B_C)
\le\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\rho.
\tag{3}
\]
Uniform continuity supplies the valid box lower bound
\[
\lambda_C:=\underline q_C-\rho
\le\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B).
\tag{4}
\]
Set \(L_\varepsilon=\min_C\lambda_C\), \(U_\varepsilon=\min_C\overline q_C\), and choose \(B_\varepsilon\) from a box attaining the latter minimum.  A box containing a compact-class minimizer, (3), and (4) give
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\rho\le L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\rho.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \(U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon<\varepsilon\).  Prune only boxes certified infeasible or having a valid lower bound strictly above the incumbent upper bound.  No box meeting \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) can satisfy either condition, so the union \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) of unpruned quotient boxes contains \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  The prescribed refinement gives \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

Every stage terminates: the chart cover and subdivision depth are finite, and every requested feasibility, arithmetic, and inclusion-oracle refinement terminates by def:certified-input-interface.  The finite record is exactly \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\) of def:certified-output.  Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in (5) and the mesh bound proves convergence of both certified gaps.  The construction is instance dependent and supplies neither a uniform complexity bound nor an SDP reduction. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Let \(E_1,E_0\) be compact metric spaces.  Under weak convergence of an ordered pair of marginal probability measures, the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in the weak topology.  Consequently, for every continuous function \(\varphi:E_1\times E_0\to\mathbb R\), the minimum and maximum of \(H\mapsto\int\varphi\,dH\) over the coupling set vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair, and the associated optimizer correspondences are upper hemicontinuous.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1. Let X and Y be separable metrizable spaces and let φ : P(X) × P(Y) ⇉ P(X × Y) be defined: φ(μ,ν) = {τ ∈ P(X × Y) | τ_X = μ, τ_Y = ν}. The correspondence φ is continuous. According to Berge's maximum theorem, if W and Z are topological spaces and Φ : W ⇉ Z is a continuous correspondence with nonempty compact values, and f : W × Z → ℝ is continuous then (i) the function m(w) = max_{z∈Φ(w)} f(w,z) is continuous, and (ii) the correspondence β defined by β(w) = {z ∈ Z | f(w,z) = m(w)} is upper-hemicontinuous.
