Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) be the unquotiented positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, and let \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).  Then \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) is surjective, and
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C=B\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)
\quad\text{for some }t_1t_0\ne0.
\]
For every such diagonal \(T\), every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), and every \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\),
\[
g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
\ell_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=\ell_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
w(q_Z(BT))=w(q_Z(B)).
\]
Consequently, for every nonempty \(K\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), the infima and suprema of each displayed pullback criterion over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) equal those over \(K\), and every attained optimizer correspondence is the inverse image of its quotient correspondence.  This theorem concerns only the rank-two restriction; the published pseudoinverse strata are carried by \(\mathcal B_Z^+\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Positive definiteness makes both arm columns nonzero, so the quotient map from \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) onto \(\mathcal B_Z\) is well defined and surjective.  The projective equivalence relation gives
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)\Longleftrightarrow C=BT,
\qquad T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0),\quad t_1t_0\ne0.
\tag{1}
\]
For such \(T\),
\[
S_{BT}=T^\top S_BT,
\qquad S_{BT}^{-1}=T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^\top)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Substitution in the trace formula and cyclicity cancel every factor of \(T\), proving \(g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c)\).  The uncontrolled term is basis independent, so the residual and worst-endpoint loss are invariant as well.  Any invariant function is constant on every fiber of a surjection; its extrema over an inverse image equal those over the quotient set, and an attained optimizer pulls back exactly to the inverse image of the quotient optimizer set.  This is an exact transfer for the positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's larger published pseudoinverse class. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).  Def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  Mutual exclusivity implies
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}=\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Exposure positivity permits division, so symmetry gives \(\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)=-2n\).  Therefore
\[
h(c)=h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=h(0)+2c/n.
\]
Subtracting the endpoint gains yields the displayed formula for \(w(B)\).

To prove non-equivalence, put \(a_e=2c_e/n\) and define on a formal endpoint-gain pair \(x\)
\[
\Phi(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
\qquad \Psi(x)=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}.
\]
If \(\Phi=\Psi+K\) for all \(x\), evaluating at \((t,0)\) gives \(K=a_U\), while evaluating at \((0,t)\) for \(t\ge a_U-a_L\) gives \(K=a_L\).  This contradicts \(c_L<c_U\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:known-exposure, ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over the nonempty class \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Since \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\), one has \(nR_n\to0\); hence the feasible and oracle conditional design variances differ by \(o(n^{-1})\), and the feasible ex ante variance equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.  The pseudoinverse coefficient equals the ordinary inverse on this class; no uniform coefficient-rate assertion is made on singular ranks.
statements.justification: This is the quantitative feasible-estimator bridge: it gives a deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope for the difference between Zhao's observable Horvitz--Thompson coefficient and the oracle coefficient, uniformly over the nonempty rate-admissible class.
statements.gap: The proof adapts Zhao's fixed-basis variance-equivalence regime uniformly over a class whose coordinate envelope and nonemptiness are imposed explicitly and supplies the public finite-\(n\) remainder \(R_n\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility makes \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\) nonempty.  Index the \(N=2n\) exposure coordinates by \(j\), put \(Z_j=D_j-\pi_j\), and let \(d_n\le\overline d n^\alpha\) be the largest closed dependency neighborhood.  If a tuple of centered coordinates has a distinct index separated from all the others, its joint moment is zero.  Counting the remaining dependency-supported tuples and using \(|Z_j|\le1\) gives, for deterministic arrays \(q,r,s\),
\[
\mathbb E_\nu\left(\sum_jq_jZ_j\right)^4
\le C N^2d_n^2\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\tag{1}
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu
\left(\sum_jq_jZ_j\right)
\left(\sum_jr_jZ_j\right)
\left(\sum_js_jZ_j\right)\right|
\le C Nd_n^2\lVert q\rVert_\infty\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, a contributing four-tuple either contains two dependency edges, giving at most \(CN^2d_n^2\) choices, or has a connected distinct-index graph, giving at most \(CN d_n^3\le CN^2d_n^2\); a contributing triple has at most \(CN d_n^2\) choices.

Fix a bounded exposure-potential-outcome array and \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  Known exposure is used at the precise disputed step: on \(D_{i,a}=1\), ass:known-exposure gives \(Y_i(W)=Y_i(a)\).  Therefore, for the signed coordinate \(Y_j\),
\[
\mathbb E_\nu\widehat Y_j^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_j,
\qquad
\{\Pi^{-1}(\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-Y)\}_j
=\frac{Y_jZ_j}{\pi_j^2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the term \(D_{i,a}\{Y_i(W)-Y_i(a)\}/\pi_{i,a}^2\) is identically zero, rather than silently dropped.  On this rank-two class Zhao's pseudoinverse is ordinary, and
\[
G_B:=\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)-\gamma_B^*(Y)
=\sum_{j=1}^{N}u_{B,j}Z_j,
\qquad
u_{B,j}=S_B^{-1}B^\top\Omega e_j\frac{Y_j}{\pi_j^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every column of \(\Omega\) has at most \(d_n\) nonzero entries, each bounded by one.  The coordinate envelope, probability-rate bound, and \(S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\) imply
\[
\sup_{B,j}\lVert u_{B,j}\rVert_2
\le K_u n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}.
\tag{5}
\]
Also
\[
X_B=n^{-1}B^\top(D-\mathbb E_\nu D)
=\sum_jx_{B,j}Z_j,
\qquad
\sup_{B,j}\lVert x_{B,j}\rVert_2\le\overline a/n.
\tag{6}
\]
Applying (1) coordinatewise gives
\[
\sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\lVert G_B\rVert_2^4
\le K_Gn^{6\alpha+8\beta-2},
\qquad
\sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\lVert X_B\rVert_2^4
\le K_Xn^{2\alpha-2}.
\tag{7}
\]
The feasible and oracle estimators satisfy
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}=\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}+\Delta_B,
\qquad \Delta_B=-G_B^\top X_B,
\]
so Cauchy--Schwarz and (7) yield
\[
\sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\Delta_B^2
\le K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}.
\tag{8}
\]

Put \(T_B=\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}-\tau\).  Equation (3) makes the Horvitz--Thompson part unbiased, and the control statistic is centered, so \(\mathbb E_\nu T_B=0\).  Write
\[
T_B=\sum_jt_{B,j}Z_j,
\qquad
t_{B,j}=n^{-1}\{Y_j/\pi_j-B_{j\cdot}\gamma_B^*(Y)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The projector inequality
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)^\top S_B\gamma_B^*(Y)
\le Y^\top\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\tag{10}
\]
and the row-sparsity, boundedness, probability, and \(\kappa\)-bounds imply
\[
\sup_B\lVert\gamma_B^*(Y)\rVert_2\le K_\gamma n^{\alpha/2+\beta},
\qquad
\sup_{B,j}|t_{B,j}|\le K_tn^{\alpha/2+\beta-1}.
\tag{11}
\]
Expanding the signed covariance and applying (2), (5), (6), and (11) gives
\[
\sup_B|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(T_B,\Delta_B\mid Y)|
\le K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (8) and (12) in the variance expansion proves the first uniform bound with
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Since \((7/2)\alpha+3\beta\le4\alpha+4\beta\), (13) is bounded by \(K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}\).

Finally, completing the square for the fixed oracle coefficient gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=n^{-2}Y^\top\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega BS_B^{-1}B^\top\Omega\Pi^{-1}\}Y.
\tag{14}
\]
Under ass:iid-potential-pairs, \(\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}(YY^\top)=Q(c_H)\).  Taking the trace expectation in (14) yields exactly
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)=h(c_H)-g_B(c_H)=\ell_B(c_H).
\tag{15}
\]
Integrating the first bound and using (15) proves the second.  Ass:zhao-first-order-rate gives \(nR_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-1}\to0\).  All inner variances are conditional design variances; the outer expectation is only the declared ex ante evaluation. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:known-exposure, ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, and ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, and put
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments,
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence \(nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) in \(L^1\) implies first-order plug-in accuracy for both regular rank-two criteria.  The condition \(\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}/n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}\to\infty\) is sufficient.  Known exposure is carried for closure with the observable estimator; the matrix-rate calculation itself is pilot only.
statements.justification: This lemma derives the pilot-size requirement needed to make robust and zero-covariance basis selection accurate on the first-order design-variance scale over a nonempty rate class.
statements.gap: The explicit factor-two matrix comparison prevents endpoint covariance error from being silently reused as a zero-covariance moment-matrix bound.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(m=m_1\wedge m_0\).  For laws \(R,S\) on \([0,1]\),
\[
\int_0^1|R^{-1}(u)-S^{-1}(u)|\,du
=\int_0^1|R(y)-S(y)|\,dy.
\tag{1}
\]
Jensen and the binomial variance formula imply
\[
\mathbb E_PW_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)
\le\frac{1}{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The first two moments and variances have the same order.  Since \(|xy-x'y'|\le|x-x'|+|y-y'|\) on \([0,1]^4\), both quantile-coupling products, and hence both covariance endpoints, have \(L^1\) error \(O(m^{-1/2})\).  Each block of \(\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) is such a scalar times \(I_n\) or \(\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), whose operator norms are one and \(n\).  Therefore
\[
M_n:=\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}(n/\sqrt m).
\tag{3}
\]

Define
\[
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\quad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^\top\Omega B)^{-1}B^\top\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
For \(Z=\Omega^{1/2}B\), \(Z(Z^\top Z)^{-1}Z^\top\) is a projector, so
\[
0\preceq A_B\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}}.
\tag{4}
\]
Dependency neighborhoods make each row of \(\Omega\) have at most \(\overline d n^\alpha\) nonzero entries, and the probability condition gives \(\lVert\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\underline\pi^{-1}n^\beta\).  Hence
\[
\lVert A_B\rVert_*\le\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*
\le2\overline d\,\underline\pi^{-2}n^{1+\alpha+2\beta},
\tag{5}
\]
which proves \(C_n=O(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1})\).  Trace duality and the one-Lipschitz property of the maximum now give
\[
\sup_B|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\le C_nM_n.
\tag{6}
\]

For the zero-covariance matrix, write \(\Delta_e=\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\), \(d_e=\widehat c_e-c_e\), and \(E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix}\).  Affinity gives
\[
\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)=\Delta_e+d_eE.
\tag{7}
\]
The off-diagonal block of \(\Delta_e\), compressed to a unit vector orthogonal to \(\mathbf1\), has eigenvalue \(-d_e\); since \(n\ge3\), \(|d_e|\le\lVert\Delta_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Thus
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2M_n,
\]
and trace duality proves the two displayed gain bounds.  Therefore \(nC_nM_n\to0\) in \(L^1\) gives first-order uniform accuracy.  Equations (3) and (5) show that the displayed pilot-growth condition is sufficient.  Ass:known-exposure is not needed for this pilot-only matrix algebra; it enters only in the downstream observable-estimator bridge. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Define \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\) by \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\).  This map is a well-defined bijection from \(\mathcal B_Z\) onto
\[
 \{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)=2\}.
\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),
 \qquad \ell_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=\ell_B(c),
 \qquad w^+(\iota(B))=w(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), both arm columns are nonzero, and \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=2\).  On this stratum the equivalence relation of def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain is exactly the independent nonzero rescaling relation defining \(\mathcal B_Z\).  Hence \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\) is well defined and injective.  Conversely, a rank-two positive-semidefinite \(S_B\) is positive definite, so its class has a unique preimage in \(\mathcal B_Z\).  On rank two, \(S_B^+=S_B^{-1}\).  Substitution into the two gain definitions proves equality of gains; subtraction from the same \(h(c)\) and endpoint maximization prove equality of losses. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\) and \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfies
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
 \qquad P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top},
\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  If \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), then for every singular \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) there is a sequence \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\) such that
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}w(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), congruence and exposure positivity give
\[
A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0.
\]
With \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\), cyclicity of trace gives
\[
n^2g_B^+(c_e)
=\operatorname{tr}\{Z_B(Z_B^\top Z_B)^+Z_B^\top A_e\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The singular-value decomposition shows that \(P_B=Z_B(Z_B^\top Z_B)^+Z_B^\top\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), with rank \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\).  The rank-two assertion follows from lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification.

For a singular representative \(B^\circ\), choose any rank-two representative \(C^\circ\) and put \(B_t^\circ=B^\circ+tC^\circ\).  The determinant of \((Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})^\top(Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})\) is a nonzero polynomial, so there is \(t_j\downarrow0\) avoiding its finitely many roots.  Normalize the two nonzero columns and call the resulting ordinary classes \(B_j\).  A convergent subsequence of their rank-two projectors has limit \(P_\infty\) whose range contains \(\operatorname{range}(Z_{B^\circ})\); hence \(P_\infty-P_B\succeq0\).  Since \(A_e\succeq0\), (1) yields
\[
\lim_jg_{B_j}(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_\infty A_e)
\ge g_B^+(c_e)
\quad(e=L,U).
\]
Subtracting from the basis-independent uncontrolled terms and taking the endpoint maximum proves \(\limsup_jw(B_j)\le w^+(B)\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every rational or real-algebraic moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), a rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure terminates and returns rational or real-algebraic bounds and a published-class basis \([B_\varepsilon]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfying
\[
L_\varepsilon^+\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le U_\varepsilon^+,
\qquad U_\varepsilon^+-L_\varepsilon^+\le\varepsilon,
\qquad w^+(B_\varepsilon)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\]
The procedure splits \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\), represents the pseudoinverse objective by rational semialgebraic formulas on each stratum, and returns a finite checkable CAD sign, sample, and value-isolation certificate covering all strata.  The set \(\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty and semialgebraic.  No exact minimizer, outer convergence to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), uniform complexity bound, or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(K_0\) be the ordered field generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the finitely many entries of \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(Q(c_L)\), and \(Q(c_U)\), together with the other exactly encoded input constants.  The rational or real-algebraic input condition in def:certified-input-interface makes every element of \(K_0\) real algebraic.  By ass:exposure-positivity, every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) is strictly positive.  Thus \(\Pi^{-1}\) exists, and its entries belong to \(K_0\).  The endpoint matrices \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\) and the design covariance \(\Omega\) are positive semidefinite by their declared spaces.  These observations supply the support, division, and positivity conditions used below.

\emph{Normalized semialgebraic representation of the quotient.}
The object \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain.  By def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain, every quotient class has a representative for which each arm column is either zero or has squared Euclidean norm \(n\).  It therefore suffices to work on
\[
 \mathcal K
 =\left\{(b_1,b_0):
   \bigl(b_1=0\ \vee\ b_1^{\top}b_1=n\bigr),\quad
   \bigl(b_0=0\ \vee\ b_0^{\top}b_0=n\bigr)
  \right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is a union of four compact semialgebraic sets over \(K_0\).  If literal quotient coordinates are desired, select, for each nonzero arm, the first nonzero coordinate and require it to be positive.  The resulting finite collection of semialgebraic sign charts is a one-to-one cross-section of the independent-rescaling quotient.  Hence any semialgebraic subset described below on normalized representatives is also semialgebraic in these quotient charts.

The objective is constant on the quotient fibers.  To verify this even at singular ranks, let \(C=\Omega^{1/2}B\), and, for \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let
\[
 R_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}.
\]
The square roots are proof intermediates only; the algorithm below uses polynomial formulas in the encoded entries.  Since \(S_B=C^{\top}C\), cyclicity of trace and def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss give
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)
 =n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
 C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}R_e
 \right].
\tag{2}
\]
If \(C=U\Sigma V^{\top}\) is a singular-value decomposition, then
\[
 C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}
 =U\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(\mathbf 1\{\sigma_j>0\}\bigr)U^{\top},
\]
the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}(C)\).  Independent nonzero rescaling of the nonzero arm columns leaves this column space unchanged.  Thus (2), and consequently \(w^+(B)\), is quotient invariant at ranks zero, one, and two.  Moreover,
\[
 0\preceq C(C^{\top}C)^+C^{\top}\preceq I,
 \qquad R_e\succeq0.
\]
Taking traces after multiplying by \(R_e\), and observing that \(n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(R_e)=h(c_e)\), yields
\[
 0\le g_B^+(c_e)\le h(c_e),
 \qquad
 0\le \ell_B^+(c_e)\le h(c_e).
\tag{3}
\]
The attainable loss set is therefore bounded below.  It is nonempty and finite because the all-zero representative belongs to \(\mathcal K\), has gain zero, and has finite endpoint losses.

\emph{Exact rank-stratified graph.}
Write \(S=S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).  Since \(\Omega\succeq0\), the matrix \(S\) is a \(2\times2\) positive-semidefinite matrix for every representative.  Its possible ranks and Moore--Penrose inverses are exactly
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\operatorname{rank}(S)&\text{semialgebraic condition}&S^+\\ \hline
0&\operatorname{tr}(S)=0&0,\\[2mm]
1&\operatorname{tr}(S)>0,\ \det(S)=0&
\displaystyle\frac{S}{\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2},\\[3mm]
2&\det(S)>0&
\displaystyle\frac{\operatorname{adj}(S)}{\det(S)}.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, positive semidefiniteness makes trace zero equivalent to rank zero.  At rank one, if the nonzero eigenvalue is \(\lambda=\operatorname{tr}(S)\) and \(S=\lambda uu^{\top}\) with \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\), then \(S/\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2=\lambda^{-1}uu^{\top}=S^+\).  At rank two, positive semidefiniteness and \(\det(S)>0\) give positive definiteness, so the last expression is the ordinary inverse.  Every denominator in (4) is strictly positive on its stated stratum, including arbitrarily close to a lower-rank boundary; at the boundary the appropriate lower-rank row is used instead.

For each row of (4), substitute the displayed rational expression into the two endpoint gains in def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss.  Introduce variables \(z_L,z_U,y\) for the two endpoint losses and their maximum, and impose
\[
 z_e=h(c_e)-g_B^+(c_e)\quad(e\in\{L,U\}),
 \qquad y\ge z_L,\qquad y\ge z_U,
 \qquad (y=z_L\ \vee\ y=z_U).
\tag{5}
\]
On rank one multiply gain equalities by the strictly positive quantity \(\{\operatorname{tr}(S)\}^2\); on rank two multiply them by the strictly positive quantity \(\det(S)\); no denominator is present on rank zero.  Thus (1), the relevant row of (4), and (5) become a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and strict or weak inequalities over \(K_0\).  Their union is the semialgebraic graph
\[
 \mathcal G
 =\{(b_1,b_0,y):(b_1,b_0)\in\mathcal K,\ y=w^+(B)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
This graph covers every representative and every rank, including the equality boundaries, without evaluating an inverse at a zero denominator.

\emph{Exact value isolation.}
Define the upper attainable-value set
\[
 \mathcal T
 =\left\{t\in\mathbb R:
   \exists (b_1,b_0,y)\in\mathcal G\ \text{with}\ y\le t
  \right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
By (3), this set is nonempty and bounded below, and by the definitions of \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and \(\mathcal G\),
\[
 \inf\mathcal T
 =\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
 =v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+.
\tag{8}
\]
The formula in (7) is first order over a real closed field.  Apply lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination to eliminate \(b_1,b_0,z_L,z_U,y\).  It returns an equivalent quantifier-free description of \(\mathcal T\) using finitely many polynomial sign conditions over \(K_0\).  A one-dimensional polynomial sign pattern is constant on every interval avoiding the finitely many real roots of its nonzero polynomials.  Consequently every finite boundary point of \(\mathcal T\) is a root of one of those polynomials.  Equations (3) and (8) make \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) such a finite boundary point.  Therefore \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is algebraic over \(K_0\), and hence is a real-algebraic number.

The corresponding cylindrical algebraic decomposition terminates because it starts with finitely many variables and input polynomials.  Each projection stage forms finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and resultants; exact real-algebraic root isolation produces finitely many sign cells; and lifting performs the same finite operation through finitely many coordinates.  The equivalence supplied by lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination certifies the sign decomposition.  Refine an isolating interval for the algebraic boundary \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) until its exactly checked width is at most the exactly encoded positive number \(\varepsilon\).  This returns rational or real-algebraic numbers \(L_\varepsilon^+\) and \(U_\varepsilon^+\) satisfying
\[
 L_\varepsilon^+\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le U_\varepsilon^+,
 \qquad
 U_\varepsilon^+-L_\varepsilon^+\le\varepsilon.
\tag{9}
\]
Strict positivity and exact encoding of \(\varepsilon\) ensure that the refinement test terminates.

\emph{Algebraic incumbent and finite certificate.}
Attainment was not used.  From the definition of an infimum and \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \exists [B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+
 \quad w^+(B)<v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\tag{10}
\]
Adjoin the real-algebraic constant \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) to the coefficient field and apply CAD lifting to the formula in (10), represented by (1), (4), and (5).  Since the formula is nonempty, CAD returns a sample point with real-algebraic coordinates.  Its normalized representative defines a basis \([B_\varepsilon]_+\) in the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, and
\[
 w^+(B_\varepsilon)<v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 w^+(B_\varepsilon)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\tag{11}
\]
Likewise, in the finite quotient charts described after (1), the weak sublevel set
\[
 \{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon\}
\]
is semialgebraic by the same rank-stratified formulas, and it is nonempty by (10).

Finally, retain the normalized quotient-chart list, the rank condition and pseudoinverse identity from (4) on each CAD cell, the projection polynomials and sign table, the algebraic sample establishing (11), and the root-isolation data establishing (9).  Exact algebraic arithmetic checks every record.  This is a finite sign, sample, and value-isolation certificate covering ranks zero, one, and two.  The procedure supplies an \(\varepsilon\)-incumbent whether or not the infimum is attained.  It claims neither convergence of outer sets to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), nor a uniform complexity bound, nor a semidefinite-program reduction. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity.  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, let \(\widehat w_m^+(B)\) and, for \(\varepsilon_m>0\), \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) be the distinct full-class empirical objective and selector in def:pilot-plugin, and put
\[
d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}|\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|.
\]
As \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(d_m^+\to0\) almost surely and
\[
\left|\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right|
\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\]
Consequently, if \(\varepsilon_m\to0\) almost surely, then
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
The domain is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain.  No exact selector at zero tolerance, cross-rank outer-argmin convergence, or point convergence is asserted without attainment and rank-separation conditions.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The bounded armwise strong law and the quantile \(L^1\) identity used in thm:plugin-correspondence give
\[
\rho_m:=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{1}
\]
For every quotient class and endpoint, lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction gives
\[
g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
\qquad \operatorname{rank}(P_B)\le2.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(\widehat A_e\) is formed from \(\widehat Q_e\), then
\[
|\operatorname{tr}\{P_B(\widehat A_e-A_e)\}|
\le2\lVert\widehat A_e-A_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\rho_m.
\tag{3}
\]
The uncontrolled endpoint term obeys
\[
|\widehat h_e-h_e|
\le n^{-2}\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*\rho_m.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4), subtraction, and the one-Lipschitz property of the maximum imply \(d_m^+\le K\rho_m\to0\) for a finite fixed-design constant \(K\), uniformly over ranks zero, one, and two.

For arbitrary functions on the same nonempty domain, the absolute difference of their infima is at most their sup-norm distance; hence
\[
\left|\inf_B\widehat w_m^+(B)-\inf_Bw^+(B)\right|\le d_m^+.
\tag{5}
\]
By the defining epsilon inequality in def:pilot-plugin,
\[
\begin{aligned}
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
&\le\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)+d_m^+\\
&\le\inf_B\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m+d_m^+\\
&\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (1), (5), and (6) prove the asserted value consistency and regret.  The argument uses neither attainment of \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) nor continuity across rank changes, so it yields no exact or outer-argmin claim. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B)).
\]
If the middle infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
Thus the fixed-threshold values exhaust the entire maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain in value through the quotient; singular or Moore--Penrose bases remain outside this conclusion.
statements.justification: This is the exact value transfer from fixed thresholds to the quotient and then to every ordinary-invertible matrix representative.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates does not introduce the normalized threshold family or prove value exhaustion and rescaling-fiber invariance.
statements.consumer: A solver can interpret its fixed-threshold optimum as an approximation to the best value over the full well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain.

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
The possibly empty full-quotient equality set is
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, its rank-two stratum is exactly
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\iota\!\left(
\bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing,\ 
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
If the rank-two infimum is attained at \(C\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  Conversely, every rank-two point \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is an ordinary-domain minimizer and belongs to a fixed-threshold argmin whose value equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The singular equality stratum is
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
A singular equality point need not imply rank-two attainment.  No unconditional full-class attainment or singular equality point is asserted.

There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]

For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]
where \(\delta=4912/39525\).  Consequently, for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\), every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), and every \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)\),
\[
w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})<w_\xi(B_0).
\]
statements.justification: The explicit witness becomes a nondegenerate region of lawful designs and marginals, with a retained rational performance margin.
statements.gap: Neither Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates nor general dependence-robust optimization results give a strict full-correspondence comparison between the minimax and zero-covariance basis rules on an open family of network experiments.
statements.consumer: Nearby lawful network experiments inherit the guarantee that every minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance optimizer.

statements.statement:
Let \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) and suppose that, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}\ge\eta.
\]
For every sequence \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) converging to \(\xi_0\) in the relative topology of def:lawful-instance-class,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
statements.justification: This quantitative lower-semicontinuity lemma is the reusable step that turns an exact optimizer-wide slack certificate into a uniform dominance margin.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals supplies continuity of the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence; the new step propagates that continuity through the moving regular projective feasible set and both optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: The triangle neighborhood corollary uses the lemma to preserve half of the exact rational separation margin.

statements.statement:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.

For every rational or real-algebraic input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the algebraic projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a locally checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.

Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.  These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.
statements.justification: This theorem derives nonempty measurable pilot selectors, finite pilot-selection regret, and a deterministic feasible-estimator variance bridge before taking the first-order limit.
statements.gap: The zero-surrogate finite-\(n\) conclusion uses a bounded deterministic linear error bound between nominal-gain regret and worst-loss deficit; outer argmax consistency alone is insufficient on the \(n^{-1}\) scale.

statements.statement:
For every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the ordinary-inverse loss has the exact intercept--slope form
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\]
Suppose the ordinary-domain zero-covariance and minimax extrema are attained.  Then
\[
\Delta_Z=
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
-\left[a^\star-\inf_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)\right].
\]
Consequently strict ordinary-domain improvement holds if and only if \(\Delta_Z>0\), equivalently if and only if there is \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) for which
\[
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\]
Thus some slope-penalty advantage must strictly exceed the sacrificed zero-covariance gain.  Through \(q_Z\), all displayed values are unchanged on \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), and every attained optimizer correspondence there is exactly the inverse image of its projective correspondence.  No universal strictness, minimax interchange, singular completion, or semidefinite reduction is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem gives the exact ordinary-inverse frontier for when copula-robust residual minimization strictly improves on the zero-covariance optimizer set.
statements.gap: The infimum formulation remains valid on the noncompact positive-definite ordinary domain and isolates precisely the slope-penalty advantage needed to offset sacrificed nominal gain.

statements.statement:
Assume ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.  Neither the optimizer-containment condition nor a primitive theorem yielding uniformly bounded \(L_n\) is proved here; both are separate checkable hypotheses.  The proposition concerns the positive-definite rank-two restriction only.
statements.justification: This proposition converts the ordinary-domain population gap into an end-to-end finite-\(n\) lower bound for two well-defined feasible pilot-selected deployments and supplies a directly checkable strictness condition.
statements.gap: It remains a conditional transfer theorem on the normalized nonempty rate-admissible class and does not turn the fixed triangle witness into an unjustified replicated-network asymptotic family.
statements.consumer: The result is the operational design-side finite-\(n\) diagnostic for independent-pilot deployment.

statements.statement:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness whose strict separation survives every singular stratum in the note's quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented pseudoinverse domain.  Let \(n=3\), \(G\), \(\nu\), and \(f_i\) be the triangle network, Bernoulli \((1/3)\) assignment, and exposure maps displayed in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate, and take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(\kappa=1/8\).  The exact matrices and endpoints are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\quad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3\end{bmatrix},
\quad c_L=-\frac14,\quad c_U=\frac14,
\]
with the two endpoint matrices displayed in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate.  The complete rank-two equality sets are
\[
\mathcal A_0=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^\top x=\mathbf1^\top y=x^\top y=0\},
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^\top x=x^\top y=0,\ (\mathbf1^\top y)^2=216/55\}.
\]
They lie in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), have normalized smallest eigenvalue \(4/27\), and satisfy
\[
\max g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
\qquad w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
On the note's quotient of the full published carrier,
\[
\mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
\[
\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)=\frac{2613}{8432},
\]
and there are no singular optimizer ties.  Consequently \(\delta=4912/39525\) and \(\eta=5/216\) give the full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide regularity slack.

For the triangle matrices displayed in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, the rank-zero and rank-one strata induced by Zhao's published unquotiented pseudoinverse carrier and expressed in the note's quotient obey
\[
\sup_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
More precisely, rank zero has \(g_B^+(0)=0\) and \(w^+(B)=171/200\).  In rank one, after normalizing the unique nonzero arm vector to squared norm three and writing \(u\) for the squared sum of its coordinates, \(0\le u\le9\), the focal-only stratum has
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)},
\]
and the comparison-only stratum has
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
\qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)}.
\]
These formulas and \(0\le u\le9\) are an exact semialgebraic certificate.

For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U).
\]
Throughout \(\mathcal U\), the optimizer correspondences on the note's quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented pseudoinverse domain contain no singular classes and satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_0(\xi)),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)).
\]
Consequently every fixed-\(\kappa\) rank-two minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every fixed-\(\kappa\) zero-covariance optimizer, and the same holds for every pair of optimizers on that full quotient, with each difference exceeding \(\delta/2\).

For the triangle instance of thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, optimization over the full maximal well-defined unquotiented ordinary-inverse domain \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) has
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}g_{q_Z(B)}(0)=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are exactly the displayed normalized equality sets in that theorem.  Their values are respectively \(31/80\) and \(2613/8432\); every zero-covariance optimizer has worst-copula loss \(521/1200\), so the exact worst-loss reduction is
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{4912}{39525}>0.
\]
Thus the triangle separation holds on the entire ordinary-inverse matrix domain implicit in Zhao's Equation (8), with optimizer sets enlarged only by independent nonzero column rescaling.  The separate singular-stratum conclusions concern only the note's novel Moore--Penrose completion.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

related_work: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates is the direct anchor. Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21 regulates a supplied basis, Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22 supplies the i.i.d. potential-outcome-pair model, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23 give the covariance-dependent basis optimization, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 gives the zero-covariance surrogate; Theorem 3 is limited to estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics. AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance is imported background: Lemma 1 proves the sharp covariance range and its quantile-coupling attainment, while Proposition 1 establishes endpoint estimation. The product coupling \(F_1\otimes F_0\) is feasible and has covariance zero, so Zhao's surrogate is an ordinarily typed member of the same covariance domain. MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment informs empirical marginal-endpoint consistency through Proposition 1, but neither supplies the independent unpaired product sampling law nor treats interference and an ex ante basis argmax. Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals informs continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences. Reeves1975GlobalQuadratic and AdjimanDallwigFloudasNeumaier1998AlphaBB inform the incumbent, region-bound, subdivision, and convex-underestimator logic, but do not cover the projective quotient, exact regularity boundary, or endpoint kink. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference; its object is the variance bound rather than the control-variate basis. GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust informs the decision-theoretic treatment of dependence ambiguity but studies generic stochastic losses. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-mapping design foundation. CaiDeJanvrySadoulet2015 is the application source for the Jiangxi insurance network that Zhao reanalyzes.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve fractions \(521/1200\), \(2613/8432\), and \(4912/39525\) are not formal claims because the triangle exposure truth tables, the resulting entries of \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), the value of \(\kappa\), full equality-set bounds, and optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack certificate are not supplied. The early kill test is oeq:separated-lawful-witness over exact assignment enumeration and both full optimizer correspondences. Unnumbered sanity check and regression test: if \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are point masses, then the definitions give \(c_L=c_U=0\), hence \(r(B)=g_B(0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R=\mathcal A_0\). Zhao's Corollary 3 supports the stronger noiseless inverse-probability-weighted basis special case, while this correspondence equality is only a definitional code check and carries no theorem or novelty status.
honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
